items.name: Fermented idli-dosa batter
items.prabhava: Overnight fermentation predigests rice and urad — the steamed result (idli) is among the lightest ways to eat grain-legume together.
combinations: ginger to balance the sour edge
items.preparation: Soak rice and urad dal separately, grind, ferment overnight; steam as idli (lightest) or griddle as dosa. Fresh, mildly sour batter is best — sharply sour batter aggravates pitta.

items.name: Rice kanji (fermented gruel)
items.prabhava: Classical aranala — sour fermented gruel that kindles agni, relieves fatigue and works as a probiotic cooler in the hot working day.
combinations: with shallot and green chili (folk style)
items.preparation: Cooked rice soaked overnight in water in a clay pot, lightly fermented; drunk next morning with the soaking water, salt and curd or buttermilk.

items.name: Meat broth (mamsa rasa)
items.prabhava: The classical convalescent food — brimhana (bulk-building) and balya (strengthening) in a form even a weak agni can digest.
combinations: ginger, black pepper and rock salt in the broth
contraindications: kapha excess with ama (unless well spiced)
items.preparation: Simmer goat meat (traditionally) long and slow with ginger, pepper and salt; strain and sip warm. Charaka prescribes it after illness, wasting and for the postpartum period.

items.name: Goat liver
items.prabhava: Raktavardhaka — classical organ-for-organ nourishment of blood; the traditional food for pallor and postpartum depletion.
combinations: cooked with turmeric, ginger and black pepper
items.preparation: Lightly cook — overcooking makes it hard and harder to digest. Small portions with warming spices, at midday when agni is strongest.

items.name: Trotters soup (paya)
items.prabhava: Gelatin-rich joint broth — sandhi (joint) and asthi (bone) nourishing by tradition; the winter-morning restorative of North India.
combinations: ginger, garlic and garam masala in the simmer
with tandoori roti or khameeri bread
items.preparation: Goat trotters simmered 4–8 hours with warming spices until the collagen melts into the broth; drunk hot, traditionally at winter dawn.

items.name: Minced mutton (keema)
combinations: fresh coriander and lemon to lift the heaviness
viruddha: with milk or milk desserts at the same meal
items.preparation: Mince cooks faster and digests a little easier than cubed meat; brown with onion, ginger, garlic and spice, and keep portions moderate — midday, in the cold seasons.

items.name: Egg bhurji
combinations: onion, tomato, green chili, turmeric (the classic masala)
viruddha: with milk at the same meal
items.preparation: Eggs scrambled soft into a spiced onion-tomato base; turmeric and coriander offset the heaviness. Better as a morning or midday protein than at night.

items.name: Plain paratha
combinations: a little fresh curd at midday
ajwain in the dough aids digestion
items.preparation: Layered wheat flatbread cooked with ghee or oil on the tawa; ghee-roasted is more sattvic than oil-fried. One or two at midday when agni can handle the richness.

items.name: Puri
items.prabhava: Festival bread — deep-frying makes wheat markedly heavier and kapha-provoking; classical texts class fried foods as occasional, not daily.
combinations: with aloo sabzi or chana (festival pairing)
items.preparation: Wheat dough rounds deep-fried until puffed. Reserve for festivals and strong midday agni; reheated or stale puris are heavier still.

items.name: Jowar bhakri
combinations: ghee or white butter smeared on top (offsets dryness)
items.preparation: Sorghum flour patted flat by hand and roasted on the tawa. Cooling and light — the farmer's summer bread; always add a fat for vata types.

items.name: Methi thepla
items.prabhava: Fenugreek-spiced travel bread — the methi bitters keep it digestion-friendly for days, which is why it is Gujarat's journey food.
contraindications: fresh-bread-only digestion — day-old theplas are drier
items.preparation: Whole-wheat dough kneaded with fresh methi leaves, turmeric, chili and curd, rolled thin and roasted with oil. Keeps 2–3 days — the classic tiffin bread.

items.name: Khakhra
combinations: a smear of ghee (softens the dryness)
methi or jeera flavours aid digestion
contraindications: vata excess / dry constitution (always add ghee)
items.preparation: Thin wheat rotis slow-roasted until crisp and moisture-free. Light kapha-friendly snack; vata types should eat it ghee-smeared, not plain.

items.name: Sambar
items.prabhava: Toor dal, tamarind, vegetables and a deepana spice blend in one pot — a complete rasa-balanced accompaniment that carries rice and idli alike.
combinations: drumstick and ash gourd as the classic vegetables
items.preparation: Toor dal simmered with tamarind, vegetables and sambar powder, finished with a mustard-curry leaf tempering. Fresh and hot; reheated sambar sours further.

items.name: Rasam
items.prabhava: Pepper-tamarind digestive soup — deepana and pachana; the traditional course that re-kindles agni mid-meal and clears monsoon congestion.
combinations: sipped after the sambar course (South Indian meal order)
extra pepper and cumin for colds
contraindications: high pitta (halve the pepper and tamarind)
items.preparation: Thin tamarind broth boiled with rasam powder (pepper, cumin, coriander), tomato and hing, finished with curry leaves. Drink hot — its virtue is in the heat and the spice.

items.name: Kadhi
items.prabhava: Direct descendant of the classical takra (buttermilk) preparations — soured buttermilk thickened with besan and tempered; grahi and digestion-friendly.
combinations: extra ginger and curry leaf for kapha
contraindications: skin conditions aggravated by sour dairy
items.preparation: Sour buttermilk or curd whisked with besan, simmered with turmeric and a ghee tempering of mustard, cumin, hing and curry leaves. A midday dish by classical takra logic.

items.name: Dal fry (toor)
contraindications: vata excess / gas (use hing and ghee generously)
items.preparation: Toor dal pressure-cooked soft, then tempered with ghee, cumin, hing, garlic and turmeric. The tempering is not garnish — it is what makes the dal digestible.

items.name: Curd rice
items.prabhava: Classical dadhyodana — cooling, grahi (stool-binding) comfort food; the traditional meal-ender of the South and the traveler's safe dish.
viruddha: curd with fresh fruit mixed in (banana especially)
items.preparation: Soft-cooked rice folded with fresh curd and a little milk, tempered with mustard, ginger and curry leaves. Midday only — curd after sunset is classically discouraged.

items.name: Lemon rice
combinations: peanuts and cashews in the tempering
items.preparation: Cooked rice tossed in a turmeric-mustard-chana dal tempering and finished off-heat with fresh lemon juice — added off the flame so the sour stays bright, not bitter.

items.name: Tamarind rice (puliyodarai)
items.prabhava: Temple prasadam of the South — the concentrated tamarind-sesame paste preserves the rice for a day's journey, the original travel meal.
combinations: peanuts and sesame in the pulikachal paste
contraindications: joint inflammation aggravated by sour (folk caution)
items.preparation: Rice mixed with pulikachal — tamarind simmered thick with sesame oil, chana dal, chilies and jaggery. Intense and sour; balance with a cooling curd course.

items.name: Coconut rice
combinations: with a pepper-forward rasam (balances the cooling)
items.preparation: Fresh grated coconut folded into rice with a ghee tempering of urad dal, mustard and curry leaves. Summer festival dish — cooling, rich, best at midday.

items.name: Vegetable pulao
combinations: whole garam masala in the ghee
seasonal vegetables — gourds keep it lightest
contraindications: none specific — portion and oil quantity decide its heaviness
items.preparation: Basmati rice sautéed in ghee with whole spices and seasonal vegetables, then steamed. A balanced one-pot meal; ghee-based and gently spiced versions suit all doshas.

items.name: Sabudana khichdi
items.prabhava: The fasting-day staple of Maharashtra — yet pure starch with peanuts and ghee is one of the heavier 'fasts'; satisfying, not light.
combinations: lemon and coriander to cut the starch
items.reviewNote: Folk status as 'light fasting food' conflicts with its guna profile (heavy, starch-dense); authored as heavy per substance, with the fasting context noted.
items.preparation: Tapioca pearls soaked till translucent, tossed with ghee, cumin, green chili, potato and crushed peanuts. Soak properly and eat warm — gummy sabudana is far harder to digest.

items.name: Kanda poha
combinations: lemon, coriander and fresh coconut on top
with masala chai — the Maharashtrian morning
contraindications: very weak agni (dry flattened rice can sit) — keep it moist and warm
items.preparation: Flattened rice rinsed soft, folded into a turmeric-mustard-onion tempering with peanuts. Light, quick morning grain — the standard against which breakfasts are measured in Maharashtra.

items.name: Dhokla
items.prabhava: Fermented and steamed — two lightening processes stacked; among the lightest ways to eat besan.
combinations: mustard-sesame-curry leaf tempering with a little sweet water
contraindications: vata excess in large amounts (besan is drying)
items.preparation: Fermented besan (or rice-chana) batter steamed into a sponge, then tempered. Naturally fermented batter digests best; instant soda versions trade lightness for bloat.

items.name: Uttapam
items.preparation: Thick fermented dosa-batter pancake griddled soft with vegetable topping — softer and moister than dosa, gentler on vata. Fresh batter over sharply soured.
